I am 70 years old and have been farming this land in Quzhou for over 50 years. My land is flat, the soil is loamy, and I know every mu of it. I am old enough that my son helps me during harvest, and I rely on machinery hired from the village cooperative for plowing and seeding. I have a high school education and I read the county extension bulletins carefully.

**My reasoning:**

The wheat-corn double rotation is what this land is built for. I will not experiment at my age — I need reliable income. I have 9 mu of land. I planted wheat here last year on all of it and I will do the same this year. After the June wheat harvest, I immediately go into summer corn on the same 9 mu. This is what every serious farmer in Quzhou does because the calendar fits perfectly and markets are stable.

For wheat, I use a certified improved variety adapted to Hebei — something like Jimai 22 or a county-recommended cultivar. The county bulletins have pushed for reduced nitrogen over the past few years due to groundwater concerns, so I will apply 14 kg of pure nitrogen per mu — split between base application at sowing and topdressing at jointing. I irrigate three times: once before sowing to settle the seedbed (winter water 越冬水), once at jointing, and once at heading. I use rotary tillage after corn to incorporate the stubble.

For corn, I use a hybrid — Xianyu 335 or similar, which yields reliably here. Summer rain in Hebei covers most of the corn's water needs, but I will keep one irrigation ready for silking if August is dry. I do no-tillage direct seeding right after wheat harvest to preserve moisture and get the plants in fast. Nitrogen is heavier on corn, split between base and topdressing at the big flare leaf stage.

My pesticide use is minimal but not zero — I spray herbicide on wheat in November and control aphids and powdery mildew once in May. On corn I do one integrated spray for armyworm and rust if pressure appears.
